LOW: RESULTS' G-A detail ('384/384 ... negative control rejected') is backed by no saved receipt. TF_RAW's detail string is hardcoded after template_selftest() returns (it would raise SystemExit on failure), so the pass itself is inferred valid.

caveats: Bootstrap CI bounds differ from ANALYSIS at the 3rd-4th decimal. analyse.py sorts ids and draws from one sequential rng stream for every statistic; I reuse one index matrix and re-seed per family. No registered outcome changes because of this.
G-A and the 'separate model load' in G-C are taken from the record and the code; no model or tokenizer was run. G-C being exactly 0.0 is consistent with deterministic FP32 with TF32 off.

The clip-threshold sensitivity (C17) is not registered. It bears on how strongly ADDITIVE should be stated, not on what was registered.

- The analyser was written after the data (raw at 16:37:42, analyser at 16:38:35).

- The denominator gate was never run.

- The 3,218 other-class rows were not scored.
- On log-odds the dose inverts: ADD-100 minus ADD-O75 is -0.0075 [-0.0126, -0.0026].

The audits' counter-reading, "Opallo's gain is 119.7% prior / entirely prior", is also an over-correction. Mismatched replies start with 2.0 nats/token more BASE headroom (5.081 vs 3.074), and gain rises with headroom (slope 0.27). My zero-forward check (VERIFIED computation, unregistered analysis) finds the sign depends on scale and covariate:
- On proportional scales the sign reverses. Relative gain is 27.6% matched vs 20.0% mismatched, and mean log(NLL_O/NLL_B) is -0.515 vs -0.261.
- Matching on headroom gives estimates from +0.364 (binned on BASE) and +0.301 (on SPARSE) through +0.067 (on the BASE/OPALLO mean) down to -0.236 (binned on OPALLO itself). Every binning carries regression-to-the-mean bias in a known direction.
- Across classes, DiD against headroom gap has r = -0.60, with an intercept of +0.29.

So this control does not identify content versus prior in either direction. The O-side result corroborates the committed d9f6b3fb finding, that Opallo carries a reply style rather than an identified skill; it does not overturn it.
